stories.headline: Trump Approves Federal Disaster Assistance for Colorado Wildfire Recovery
stories.summary:
President Trump has approved a Public Assistance designation as part of Colorado's Major Disaster Declaration, Gov. Jared Polis announced Friday. The approval unlocks federal funding to help communities across the state recover from two major wildfires that burned earlier in 2026.

Public Assistance grants can cover costs related to debris removal, emergency protective measures, and the repair or replacement of damaged public infrastructure such as roads, bridges, and public buildings. The designation is a significant step for affected communities that have been working to secure federal support.

Gov. Polis had requested the Major Disaster Declaration earlier this year as Colorado faced an exceptionally active wildfire season. The approval signals the federal government's recognition of the scale of damage sustained by Colorado communities.

stories.headline: Denver Metro Faces Another Week of 90-Degree Heat With Labor Day Storm Chances
stories.summary:
Temperatures across the Denver metro area are expected to remain in the lower 90s through Labor Day weekend, continuing a prolonged stretch of summer-like heat well into September. Scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms are possible each day, with Labor Day itself carrying the highest storm coverage risk.

Storms on the northeast plains Friday night could produce gusty winds and hail, though areas along the I-25 corridor and points west are expected to remain mostly dry. Sunday brings a slight uptick in moisture, increasing the chance of brief heavy rain and gusty winds from afternoon thunderstorms.

A modest cooldown is forecast to begin Tuesday as an upper-level ridge weakens, though temperatures are expected to remain above normal. Forecasters caution that the cooler trend may be short-lived, with warmer weather likely returning later in the week.

stories.headline: Update: Fights Erupt at Denver ICE Protest, Three Hospitalized
stories.summary:
Three people were transported to the hospital after five separate fights broke out among demonstrators gathered at Denver's La Alma-Lincoln Park on Friday afternoon. The protest was part of a planned 'ICE Out' demonstration and school walkout organized by the Colorado Youth Coalition and 50501 Colorado.

According to Denver Police spokesperson Doug Schepman, the fights occurred between 12:45 p.m. and 2 p.m. among a large group that had assembled at noon. One additional person was medically evaluated at the scene, and another left the area before officers could make contact. Police did not disclose the severity of the injuries.

Officers identified or contacted several suspects in connection with the reported assaults, though Schepman did not confirm whether any citations or arrests were made. Police noted the demonstration was unpermitted and held without a safety plan, which they said contributed to an unsafe environment. Investigations remain ongoing.

stories.headline: Community Rallies Around Denver Soul Food Owner Hospitalized After Crash With Stolen Truck
stories.summary:
Alphonso Campbell, owner of AFC Wings and Fish, remains hospitalized in critical condition following a T-bone collision with a stolen Ford F-350 near Colorado Boulevard and 35th Avenue on Aug. 28. Campbell was on his way to serve customers when the crash occurred.

Aurora Police said their officers had been pursuing the stolen truck but called off the chase when it crossed into Denver due to public safety concerns. APD confirmed APD officers were not present when the suspect struck Campbell's vehicle. Campbell faces multiple surgeries and months of recovery, according to his sister Aleea Campbell.

The Denver community has responded with an outpouring of support. A GoFundMe campaign to help cover medical expenses has raised nearly $30,000. Campbell is a former baseball coach at Northfield High School who pivoted to food entrepreneurship while remaining deeply involved in the community. His team continues to operate AFC Wings and Fish in his absence.

stories.headline: Colorado Extends Order Allowing COVID Vaccine Access Without a Doctor's Prescription
stories.summary:
Colorado health officials on Friday reissued a standing order permitting any resident six months of age or older to receive a COVID-19 booster vaccine without a doctor's prescription. The action extends a previous order that was set to expire Friday and is designed to sidestep federal policy uncertainty that has made some pharmacists hesitant to administer the shots.

The FDA has approved updated COVID vaccines for the 2026-27 season but with limitations suggesting those under 65 without underlying health conditions may not qualify under federal guidance. That restriction led major pharmacy chains to temporarily stop offering vaccines to many Coloradans last year until the state intervened with a similar order.

Gov. Polis said the order allows residents to make their own healthcare choices without bureaucratic delays or a required physician visit. State Board of Pharmacy rules have since been expanded to allow pharmacists to prescribe vaccines directly. Private insurance, Medicare, and Medicaid are all expected to cover the updated boosters at no cost to patients.

stories.headline: Denver Metro Chamber CEO Says 'Poor Choices' Have Made Region Less Desirable for Business
stories.summary:
Denver Metro Chamber of Commerce CEO J.J. Ament said following the Chamber's annual meeting that a series of policy decisions have made the Denver metro area a less attractive destination for businesses and workers. Ament discussed downtown office vacancies and job market trends with CPR News, pointing to local governance and policy as contributing factors.

Ament did not detail each specific policy he criticized, but his comments reflect ongoing concerns from the business community about the region's economic competitiveness, persistent downtown vacancy rates, and quality-of-life issues that have shaped employer and worker decisions in recent years.

The remarks carry weight given the Chamber's role as one of the region's leading business advocacy organizations. Downtown Denver has continued to struggle with high commercial vacancy rates following the pandemic-era shift to remote work, and civic leaders have been debating how best to revitalize the urban core.

stories.headline: CSU Rolls Past Wyoming 35-13 in Jim Mora's Debut, Reclaims Bronze Boot
stories.summary:
Colorado State defeated Wyoming 35-13 on Saturday at Canvas Stadium in Fort Collins, giving first-year head coach Jim Mora a winning debut and returning the Bronze Boot trophy to the Rams. It was the earliest Border War matchup since 1964 and CSU's first win over Wyoming since 2024, avenging a 28-0 shutout loss in Laramie last season.

Quarterback Hauss Hejny threw five touchdown passes, connecting three times with receiver RJ Vick, who had a 57-yard scoring grab that proved to be the momentum-turning play of the game. The Rams led 14-6 at halftime, weathered a Wyoming scoring drive early in the third quarter that trimmed the deficit to 14-13, then pulled away with three unanswered touchdowns.

CSU's defense held Wyoming to just 88 yards in the second half. Linebacker Oumar Diomande recorded 11 tackles and an interception. Coach Mora praised his team's composure in responding to Wyoming's early second-half score. 'The moment wasn't too big for them,' Mora said. 'They just kept playing the next play.'

stories.headline: Rapids Fall 3-0 to Columbus Crew in Another Listless Road Performance
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rapids lost 3-0 to the Columbus Crew on Saturday at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in a match marred by a controversial opening goal, missed chances, and a defensive collapse in the closing minutes. Head coach Matt Wells said the result exposed a recurring problem: the Rapids are a fundamentally different team when they concede first.

The opening goal came from a corner kick that should not have been awarded, as Columbus forward Josef Martinez was in an offside position on the prior play. Goalkeeper Adam Beaudry failed to punch the ball clear on the corner, and Columbus headed in the rebound. The Rapids had multiple quality chances in the first half but lacked the finishing touch to convert.

Goals two and three came late, with substitute Gonzalo Tapia scoring in the 81st minute and then setting up Taja Habroune in stoppage time as Colorado pushed numbers forward. The loss continues a troubling road form for the Rapids. 'The second half was a technical disaster,' Wells said after the match.

stories.headline: Avalanche Prospect Pool Absent From Top 150 NHL Rankings, Rookie Faceoff Offers Chance to Respond
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche did not have a single player appear on The Athletic's ranking of the top 150 young players and prospects across the NHL, making them one of only two organizations — along with the Florida Panthers — to be completely absent from the list. The ranking includes players under 23 years old, from established stars like Connor Bedard down to players who have yet to debut in the NHL.

The thin prospect pool is widely attributed to Colorado's sustained win-now approach under general manager Joe Sakic, who has repeatedly traded draft picks and young talent to acquire veteran contributors. A notable example is Calum Ritchie, who was dealt to the New York Islanders as part of the Brock Nelson trade in 2025 and subsequently made the top-150 list with his new team.

Colorado's Rookie Faceoff roster has been released, with goaltender Ilya Nabokov as the most prominent name. The team will face the Anaheim Ducks and Vegas Golden Knights in the coming days, giving young Avalanche players an opportunity to challenge the perception that the organization's pipeline is bare.

stories.headline: Two Tallest Buildings in Colorado Springs Headed to Foreclosure Auction in October
stories.summary:
The two tallest buildings in Colorado Springs are scheduled to go to foreclosure auction beginning Oct. 21, marking a significant development in the ongoing struggles facing commercial real estate in the region. The properties represent a major portion of the Colorado Springs skyline and their distressed status reflects broader headwinds confronting office and mixed-use towers across Colorado.

Details on the ownership structure and the debt behind the foreclosure proceedings were not fully disclosed in available reports, but the auction date signals that efforts to refinance or sell the properties outside of foreclosure have not succeeded. The outcome of the auction is expected to have lasting implications for downtown Colorado Springs.

The situation mirrors challenges seen in Denver, where commercial office vacancy rates have remained elevated in the post-pandemic era and property values have declined. Colorado Springs civic and business leaders are watching the auction closely given the properties' prominence in the city's commercial real estate market.

stories.headline: Colorado Income Tax Overhaul Targeting Top Earners Headed to November Ballot
stories.summary:
Colorado voters will decide this November on a proposed overhaul of the state's income tax structure that would increase rates on the highest earners. The measure heads to the ballot following approval by the state legislature, setting up a major statewide tax policy debate ahead of the general election.

Colorado currently has a flat income tax rate, and any shift toward a graduated structure targeting top earners would represent a fundamental change to how the state funds government services. Supporters argue the change would make the tax code more equitable, while opponents contend it could drive high-income residents and businesses out of the state.

The measure is expected to generate significant campaign spending from both sides as Election Day approaches. It comes as Colorado also grapples with questions about revenue adequacy under the Taxpayer's Bill of Rights, which limits how much tax revenue the state can retain.

stories.headline: Poll: 8th Congressional District Voters Back Lighter Immigration Enforcement
stories.summary:
A new poll of Colorado's 8th Congressional District shows that a majority of voters in the competitive swing district favor a lighter approach to immigration enforcement. The findings are notable given that the 8th District, which covers parts of the northern Denver metro and Adams County, is considered one of the most closely watched House seats in the country.

The survey results could have implications for how both parties approach immigration messaging in the district heading into the November election. The 8th District has been represented by Democrat Yadira Caraveo and has been a top Republican target in recent election cycles.

The poll's release comes amid heightened national and local attention to immigration enforcement, following protests and school walkouts across Colorado earlier this week. Immigration has emerged as one of the defining issues of the 2026 midterm election cycle.

topStory.headline: Hurricane Lowell Threatens Hawaiian Islands With Life-Threatening Surf, Flooding
topStory.summary:
Hurricane Lowell, a powerful Category 4 storm, is bearing down on the Hawaiian island chain and is expected to produce life-threatening surf, widespread flooding, and mudslides even as its forecast track has it passing just west of the major islands by Monday night. As of Saturday, the storm was located approximately 640 miles south-southwest of Honolulu, moving west-northwest at 7 mph with sustained winds of 145 mph. The National Hurricane Center warned that Kauai could receive up to 10 inches of rain, while Maui could see up to 8 inches.

Lowell briefly intensified to Category 5 status — with sustained winds of 157 mph or greater — overnight Friday before weakening slightly into Category 4 range. The storm's projected path is expected to trigger storm watch notices for Kauai County and the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument. National Weather Service meteorologist John Bravender cautioned at a Friday news conference that proximity to the forecast cone's edge does not guarantee safety.

Hawaii Gov. Josh Green urged residents, particularly those in Kauai County, to complete emergency preparations and avoid floodwaters and dangerous surf. State officials said they are securing harbors, deploying emergency personnel to strategic locations, and monitoring dams for possible breaches or overflows. The warning comes weeks after Tropical Storm Lala brought intense flooding and strong winds to parts of Oahu and the Big Island.

Lowell is one of three simultaneous tropical cyclones active in the northern Pacific. Hurricane Karina, a former Category 4 storm, was spinning roughly 755 miles east-northeast of Hilo, while Tropical Storm Marie was churning about 705 miles west of the southern tip of Baja California. Meteorologists said Marie could generate high surf along the Southern California coast during the holiday weekend.

The three-storm cluster is part of a notably active Northeast Pacific hurricane season, which has produced 15 named storms to date, according to Colorado State University. Experts attribute the elevated activity to unusually warm sea surface temperatures and the presence of an El Niño weather pattern, which is also expected to bring potentially historic rainfall to California in the coming months.
